adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws plain Error in API handler producing 500 with non-JSON body, causing client response.json() to throw SyntaxError instead of surfacing the actual error; should return res.status(400).json(...) like other error paths

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path does `if (!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) { ... throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError); }` with no surrounding try/catch. That will produce an unhandled 500 response rather than the consistent `res.status(...).json({ error: ... })` used elsewhere in the handler. On the client, `DisableTwoFactorModal` always does `const body = await response.json();` for non-200 responses, so a non-JSON 500 body can indeed cause `response.json()` to throw and prevent surfacing the intended error code/message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal's dialog onOpenChange (X button/backdrop dismiss) bypasses resetState() and object-URL cleanup, leaving stale step/backupCodes state and leaking blob URL on reopen

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal the internal state (step/password/errorMessage/etc.) is only reset via resetState() on the explicit Cancel button and the backup-codes Close button, but the Dialog is wired as `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` with no wrapper to call resetState() when the user dismisses via the X button/backdrop (onOpenChange(false)). That means the component can reopen with a stale `step`/`backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl` from the prior session. Additionally, `backupCodesUrl` is created with `URL.createObjectURL(...)` and only revoked when a new URL is created (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), with no cleanup on dismiss/unmount, so dismissing via X/backdrop can leave the blob URL unreleased.

adjudication_records.issue_text: onEnable() is never called when dialog is dismissed via X, so parent's 2FA-enabled switch state goes stale

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable no longer calls onEnable() immediately; it now sets step to DisplayBackupCodes (handleEnable: `if (response.status === 200) { setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); return; }`). onEnable() is only invoked by the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes footer. However the Dialog can also be dismissed via the dialog’s close control (X) which triggers `onOpenChange` from the parent; this component does not wrap/intercept `onOpenChange` to call `onEnable()` (or even `resetState()`). So if the user enables 2FA, reaches the backup-codes step, and closes via X, the backend is enabled but the parent callback isn’t fired, leaving parent UI state (e.g., the switch) stale.

missing_backup_codes error tells users to generate codes in settings but no settings UI to generate/regenerate backup codes exists, creating a dead-end for users who enabled 2FA before migration or exhausted all codes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` and user-facing copy: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." (common.json). Both login (`next-auth-options.ts` throws MissingBackupCodes when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes`) and disable-2FA (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` returns MissingBackupCodes when `req.body.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes`) can hit this state. However, the only place backup codes are generated/shown is during the 2FA setup flow (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generates and stores `backupCodes`, and `EnableTwoFactorModal` displays them post-enable). The diff shows no settings UI/action to generate/regenerate backup codes for already-enabled 2FA users (e.g., pre-migration users with `backupCodes` null), making the prescribed remediation a dead end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code authentication has zero test coverage; no tests verify backup code login, single-use consumption, or replay rejection, only the download/copy buttons are tested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial backup-code auth/consumption logic (e.g., `next-auth-options.ts` checks `credentials.backupCode`, finds it in decrypted `user.backupCodes`, then marks it used via `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts/saves). However, the only added Playwright assertions around backup codes are UI-level interactions after enabling 2FA—download, copy, close (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`), and the file even includes a TODO to add backup code tests. There are no tests in the diff that exercise backup-code login, verify single-use consumption, or ensure replay is rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: LoginValues.backupCode was added to the form interface but the zod formSchema was not updated, so zodResolver strips the backupCode field before submission causing an infinite TOTP loop

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginValues` gaining `backupCode` and `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`, but it does not include the `formSchema` definition or any changes to it. Therefore, the claim that the zod schema was not updated and that `zodResolver` strips `backupCode` (causing an “infinite TOTP loop”) cannot be verified from this diff alone.

matched_golden_ids: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: backup code validation is case-sensitive, rejecting valid codes with uppercase hex characters. It additionally mentions lack of trimming, but the primary issue aligns with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Closing the backup-codes dialog via the Dialog's X / onOpenChange never calls resetState, leaving stale step state, surviving backupCodes data, and leaking object URLs via missing URL.revokeObjectURL

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, local modal state is only reset via the Cancel button (calls resetState()) and the “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. The Dialog itself is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, but `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` is passed through without invoking `resetState`, so closing via the Dialog chrome (e.g., X/overlay) can leave `step` and other state (notably `backupCodes` and `backupCodesUrl`) intact for the next open. Additionally, `resetState()` does not clear `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl` nor revoke the created object URL; `URL.revokeObjectURL` is only called when creating a new URL in `handleSetup`, not on close/reset, so an object URL can remain allocated if the dialog is closed after setup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code verification has no attempt limiting (unlike the password path), allowing brute-forcing the 2^40 hex space through repeated authorize calls; disable.ts has no limiter at all

adjudication.rationale: The new backup-code authentication/disable branches perform only a direct membership check (indexOf on decrypted backupCodes) with no rate limiting or lockout visible in the diff. In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` path verifies and updates backup codes but does not call any limiter. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` branch similarly checks the code and proceeds without any attempt limiting. This enables unlimited online guessing attempts against backup codes via repeated calls to these endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are persisted encrypted before 2FA is enabled and regenerated on every setup call, silently invalidating codes saved from a prior abandoned setup or disable-then-re-enable cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are generated and persisted during the setup call (before 2FA is enabled): `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generates `backupCodes` and stores them via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})`, and this will overwrite any existing `backupCodes` on each setup invocation. That means repeating setup (e.g., restarting the flow) will change the stored codes. However, this is not clearly a defect: regenerating secrets/codes on each setup attempt is plausible/expected behavior, and old codes being invalid after a disable/re-enable is also expected since disable sets `backupCodes: null`. The “silently invalidating” aspect is more of a UX/flow/architecture concern than a verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message tells users to regenerate backup codes in settings, but the PR includes no settings UI, API endpoint, or regeneration mechanism; users who exhaust codes must disable and re-enable 2FA

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the message `"missing_backup_codes": "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."` (en/common.json) and returns `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` from both login (next-auth authorize) and the disable endpoint when `user.backupCodes` is null. However, the PR only generates backup codes during `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` (EnableTwoFactorModal flow) and displays them once; it does not add any settings UI/action or API endpoint to regenerate backup codes while 2FA remains enabled. The only visible way to get new codes from this diff is effectively to run setup again (disable/re-enable), so the error text is potentially misleading/incomplete product behavior rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tabIndex={-1} on password-visibility toggle in Input.tsx is unrelated accessibility-affecting scope drift shipped silently in a 2FA PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated change in `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx` adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the password-visibility toggle `<button>`, which removes it from the keyboard tab order. This is an accessibility-affecting behavior change and is not directly tied to the 2FA/backup-code feature changes elsewhere in the PR, so the “scope drift shipped silently” concern is diff-grounded. Whether it is definitively a bug cannot be concluded from the diff alone (it may be intentional), but it is a substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are generated and persisted at setup (not enable), so abandoned setup attempts leave stored-but-never-displayed codes that later setup calls silently overwrite, invalidating previously downloaded codes without notice

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated and persisted immediately during setup (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)` in the Prisma update) and returned in the setup response. However, in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, those codes are not displayed to the user until after the later enable step succeeds (`setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` happens only in `handleEnable` after a 200). This means if a user starts setup (triggering `/setup`), then cancels/abandons before enabling, the DB now contains new backup codes that were never shown. Additionally, repeated setup calls overwrite `user.backupCodes` (and set `twoFactorEnabled: false`) silently, which can invalidate previously downloaded backup codes without any user-visible notice if the user doesn’t complete the flow to the display step.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Circular TextField→PasswordField swap and required attribute on DisableTwoFactorModal are unrelated drive-by fixes that should be split out or explicitly called out

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a swap in `EnableTwoFactorModal` from `TextField` (with `type="password"`) to `PasswordField` (import changed accordingly), and in `DisableTwoFactorModal` adding `required` to the existing `PasswordField`. These changes are not necessary for the core backup-code feature being added (backup code generation, display, API handling) and read as opportunistic UX/validation tweaks. That’s a scope/splitting concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Login-with-backup-code and disable-with-backup-code flows have zero test coverage; the security-critical single-use consumption logic in next-auth-options.ts ships untested (acknowledged by TODO)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new security-relevant backup-code flows and single-use consumption logic (e.g., in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` it verifies `credentials.backupCode`, finds the code, then nulls it out and re-encrypts the remaining list via `prisma.user.update`). However, the only added Playwright coverage (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) tests backup-code *display/download/copy/close* after enabling 2FA, and even contains an explicit TODO: `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. There is no test shown for logging in with a backup code or disabling 2FA using a backup code, so the newly introduced single-use consumption and disable-with-backup-code behavior ships without direct automated coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code one-time-use invariant enforced with non-atomic check-then-write (indexOf on decrypted snapshot then separate prisma.user.update), allowing the same code to authenticate concurrent logins
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race condition: a non-atomic check-then-update on decrypted backup codes, allowing concurrent login requests to both accept and consume the same backup code, breaking one-time-use semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read-modify-write of the entire backup code list lets concurrent logins with different valid codes race, overwriting each other and resurrecting already-consumed codes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login decrypts the full `user.backupCodes` array, mutates one entry (`backupCodes[index] = null`), then writes the entire re-encrypted JSON back via `prisma.user.update(...)`. This read-modify-write is not guarded by a transaction/compare-and-swap or per-code atomic update, so two concurrent logins using different valid codes can both read the same original list and then overwrite each other’s updates (last write wins), effectively resurrecting a code that the other request consumed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every setup call unconditionally regenerates and overwrites backupCodes, silently invalidating all unconsumed codes

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated on every call (`const backupCodes = ...`) and then persisted via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) ... }})` with no check for existing codes or user state. This overwrites any previously stored (and potentially unconsumed) backup codes each time the setup endpoint is hit, invalidating older codes without any explicit rotation/confirmation mechanism shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint writes live backup codes to the DB during an unenrolled state, persisting codes the user never viewed, with no committed/visible state notion

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` now generates `backupCodes` and persists them immediately (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`) while explicitly keeping `twoFactorEnabled: false` (unenrolled state). The UI doesn’t display backup codes until after `/enable` succeeds (EnableTwoFactorModal sets `backupCodes` on setup response but only renders them in `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, which is reached only after a successful enable). So the finding is accurate: codes can be stored even if the user abandons setup and never views them. This is more a design/state-management concern than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone, since codes aren’t usable unless `twoFactorEnabled` is true and a later setup will overwrite them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code client TextField only enforces minLength 10 / maxLength 11 while server normalizes by stripping dashes, so codes with whitespace or trailing newlines pass client validation but fail server-side with a misleading 'incorrect code' error

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`, the backup code field only constrains length (`minLength={10}`, `maxLength={11}`) and does not trim/normalize input. On the server, both the disable endpoint and next-auth authorize logic compare against stored codes by only stripping dashes (`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` / `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`) and do not trim whitespace. So inputs that are the right length but contain whitespace (e.g., an embedded/leading/trailing space instead of a hex character) can satisfy the client-side length constraints yet will never match server-side, resulting in an `IncorrectBackupCode` error rather than a clearer validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog X/Escape dismissal path at backup-codes step fires onCancel() but neither resetState() nor onEnable(), desyncing the settings switch state and leaving stale modal state

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable now sets `step` to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` and defers `onEnable()` until the explicit “close” button in that step (`onClick` calls `resetState(); onEnable();`). During the backup-codes step, the normal cancel button (which calls `onCancel(); resetState();`) is hidden (`step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? ... : null`). The `<Dialog>` uses only `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` and there is no shown logic to call `resetState()` or `onEnable()` when the dialog is dismissed via X/Escape/overlay close. That can leave stale internal modal state (still on DisplayBackupCodes with previous `backupCodesUrl`) and can also skip `onEnable()` even though the backend enable succeeded, potentially desyncing the settings switch/UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resetState resets password/error/step but never clears backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, or secret, leaking the Blob URL and leaving stale codes

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, `resetState` only calls `setPassword("")`, `setErrorMessage(null)`, and `setStep(SetupStep.ConfirmPassword)` but does not clear `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri`, or `secret` (see added state at lines `useState([])`, `useState("")`, etc.). `backupCodesUrl` is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and only revoked when a *new* setup succeeds (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), so closing/canceling after generating it will keep the Blob URL alive and retain stale backup codes/QR/secret in component state until unmount or the next setup. That’s a real resource leak/stale-state defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the shared PasswordField visibility toggle removes keyboard access to show/hide password for every form in the app

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`, the password visibility toggle is a `<button>` that previously could be reached via keyboard tab navigation. The diff adds `tabIndex={-1}` to that button, which removes it from the tab order, preventing keyboard-only users from focusing and activating the show/hide control across all usages of `PasswordField`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Weakened e2e assertion `isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` always passes because a Locator is always truthy, making the 2FA switch check vacuous

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the assertion was changed to `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `locator.isChecked()` returns a Promise<boolean>. Passing that Promise directly into `expect(...).toBeTruthy()` asserts the Promise object (always truthy), not the resolved boolean, so the check becomes vacuous. The added FIXME comment in the diff also notes it passes even when the switch is not checked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are generated, persisted, and returned at the setup step rather than the enable step, and re-calling setup silently overwrites previously issued codes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup codes are generated and stored during the TOTP setup API call, not during enable: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` creates `backupCodes` and immediately persists `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)` in `prisma.user.update(...)`, and returns them in the setup response (`return res.json({ ..., backupCodes })`). There is no corresponding generation/persistence in the enable step; enable just advances UI to display the already-returned codes. Because setup always writes a fresh `backupCodes` value, re-calling setup will overwrite any previously issued (but possibly saved) codes without any explicit regeneration flow or warning. This is a real, diff-grounded product/UX/security concern, though not necessarily a strictly broken behavior given setup could be treated as “regenerate codes.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code verification in disable.ts has no attempt throttling, allowing online brute force of the 40-bit backup codes to disable 2FA

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) { ... }`) performs only a direct `indexOf` match against decrypted codes and returns `IncorrectBackupCode` on failure, but there is no rate limiting / attempt throttling logic shown (no call to `checkRateLimitAndThrowError` or similar) before allowing repeated online guesses against `req.body.backupCode`. Given backup codes are generated as 10 hex chars in `setup.ts` (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`), this creates an online brute-force surface for disabling 2FA via this endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code comparison uses indexOf instead of constant-time comparison, leaking per-character timing signal on login and disable paths

adjudication.rationale: Both the login path (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts) and the disable endpoint (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts) validate a user-supplied backup code via `backupCodes.indexOf(<userInput>)`. This implies variable-time string comparisons and a linear search through the array, rather than a constant-time equality check against stored secrets. Given these are authentication/2FA gates, the diff does introduce a timing-sensitive comparison mechanism on those paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Every call to setup.ts regenerates and persists a fresh backup-code set, silently invalidating codes the user previously saved and potentially locking them out of the recovery flow

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each call generates a new `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and immediately persists it to the user via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ... } })` before 2FA is actually enabled. This overwrites any previously stored backup codes with no guard/confirmation, so if setup is re-run (e.g., user retries setup or refreshes the flow) any previously saved codes become invalid, matching the finding’s “silently invalidating” concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 2FA-enable assertion expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy() passes even when the switch is NOT checked, giving false confidence that 2FA is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the assertion `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` is not actually validating the switch state because `isChecked()` returns a Promise<boolean>; passing that Promise into `expect(...).toBeTruthy()` will be truthy regardless of the resolved boolean. The diff even adds a FIXME comment noting it “passes even when switch is not checked,” confirming the issue is present in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code e2e assertions only check surface artifacts (filename constant and success toast) rather than file content or clipboard content, so empty/malformed/wrong backup codes would pass

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts the new backup-code assertions only verify the download suggestedFilename() equals "cal-backup-codes.txt" and that clicking the copy button yields a success toast (waitFor toast-success). The test explicitly leaves content validation as TODOs ("// TODO: check file content" and "// TODO: check clipboard content"), so malformed/empty backup codes could still pass these e2e checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The backup-code login branch in next-auth-options.ts (decrypt, indexOf match, single-use consumption, re-encrypt) has no test coverage, leaving the single-use guarantee unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new backup-code branch in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` that decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, and then consumes the code by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting/saving it via `prisma.user.update(...)`. In the shown test changes (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`), there is only a TODO comment about adding backup code tests and no actual test exercising backup-code login or verifying the single-use consumption behavior. This is a specific, nontrivial new auth path lacking demonstrated coverage in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new req.body.backupCode branch in the TOTP disable endpoint is never exercised by any test

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` to handle `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` (decrypt backup codes, validate, and allow disabling 2FA). The only modified/added test shown is `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, which explicitly notes `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` and does not call the disable endpoint with a backup code. No other tests in the diff exercise that new disable-with-backup-code branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test pins down the backup-code format normalization between client display (xxxxx-xxxxx) and server validation (dash-stripping), risking silent lockouts from format mismatch

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a specific client/server normalization contract: UI displays backup codes as `XXXXX-XXXXX` via `formatBackupCode` (EnableTwoFactorModal) and accepts that format in `BackupCode` (placeholder, maxLength 11), while server-side validation strips dashes with `.replaceAll("-", "")` in both the disable API (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`) and NextAuth authorize. The Playwright suite adds coverage for showing/downloading/copying backup codes but explicitly notes missing backup-code tests and does not assert that a dashed input is accepted/normalized. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded gap in tests for newly added logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes error branches in login.tsx are untested and shadow the existing errorMessages fallback, so i18n key typos or divergent message paths ship undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, `handleTotpSubmit` adds explicit branches for `ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode` and `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` that bypass the existing `errorMessages[res.error] || t("something_went_wrong")` fallback by directly calling `t("incorrect_backup_code")` / `t("missing_backup_codes")` (lines added around the `signIn` result handling). The diff’s Playwright coverage (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) includes TODO/FIXME notes and only tests showing/copying/downloading backup codes after enabling 2FA, not login failure/success paths using backup codes or these specific error branches. This creates a real risk that i18n key typos or divergent message mappings in these new branches ship without test coverage, but it’s not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration adds backupCodes column but does not backfill codes for existing users with twoFactorEnabled = true, leaving them with no recovery path since no settings UI exists to regenerate codes and the error message points to a nonexistent flow

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup-code-based recovery flows (login “lost_access” and disable-2FA via `req.body.backupCode`), but the migration only adds `users.backupCodes` with no backfill (`ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN "backupCodes" TEXT;`). For existing users with `twoFactorEnabled = true`, `backupCodes` will remain null, and both the login authorize path and disable endpoint explicitly error (`ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes`) when `backupCodes` is absent. The UI message says “Please generate them in your settings.”, but in this diff codes are only generated during `/totp/setup` and shown after enabling 2FA, with no evident regeneration flow for already-enabled users—making the new “lost access” path a dead end for that cohort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts unconditionally overwrites backupCodes on every call, silently invalidating previously saved backup codes when a 2FA-enabled user re-runs setup

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the handler always generates a fresh `backupCodes` array and writes `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)` in the `prisma.user.update(...)` call, with no diff-shown guard based on existing `user.backupCodes`/`user.twoFactorEnabled`. So repeated calls will overwrite previously stored backup codes. Whether that’s a defect is not provable from the diff alone (it may be intended rotation on re-setup), but it is a concrete behavioral/UX/security concern worth addressing explicitly (e.g., prevent re-setup when already enabled or clearly rotate codes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single-use consumption writes null into the backupCodes array, so after all codes are used the JSON string still passes the !user.backupCodes check, causing IncorrectBackupCode instead of the intended missing_backup_codes regeneration message

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login only checks `if (!user.backupCodes)` to emit `MissingBackupCodes`, but single-use consumption sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the JSON array back into `user.backupCodes`. After all codes are consumed, `user.backupCodes` remains a non-empty encrypted string, so the missing-codes branch never triggers; instead `indexOf(...)` on an array of nulls returns `-1` and throws `IncorrectBackupCode`. The diff contains no logic to detect 'no remaining valid codes' (e.g., all null/empty) and return `MissingBackupCodes`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is burned inside authorize() before the rest of the authentication flow completes; if any later step fails, the user permanently consumed a backup code without gaining access (silent partial success)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup code is invalidated immediately inside `authorize()` by updating the user record (`backupCodes[index] = null; await prisma.user.update(...)`) right after validation. This happens before `authorize()` completes/returns successfully and without any transactional coupling to the rest of the authentication/session creation flow. If any later part of `authorize()` (or subsequent NextAuth flow after `authorize` returns) fails, the backup code will already have been consumed even though the user didn’t get logged in, matching the reported “silent partial success” risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code comparison lacks case normalization: codes are lowercase hex but the UI applies no lowercase transform, so an uppercase-typed valid code is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`), stored, and later compared via `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (and similarly `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `next-auth-options.ts`) with no case normalization. The UI input (`BackupCode.tsx`) does not force lowercase, so a user entering valid codes in uppercase (common when copying/typing) will not match and will be rejected with `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: resetForm clears the RHF field totpCode via setValue, but TwoFactor component holds per-digit input state internally, leaving digit boxes visually populated while the form value is empty after toggling 'lost access' mode

adjudication.rationale: In both places where the user can toggle “lost access” mode (Login and DisableTwoFactorModal), the UI conditionally renders either `<TwoFactor />` or `<BackupCode />`. Toggling flips `twoFactorLostAccess`, which unmounts `TwoFactor` entirely (`twoFactorLostAccess ? <BackupCode/> : <TwoFactor/>`). Since `TwoFactor` is unmounted/remounted on the toggle, its internal per-digit `useState` cannot remain visually populated across the mode switch, regardless of `form.setValue("totpCode", "")`. The alleged mismatch (RHF cleared but digit boxes still filled after toggling) isn’t supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Closing the backup-codes dialog via Dialog onOpenChange (X/Esc) skips resetState() and onEnable, leaving stale internal step state, stale parent 2FA toggle, and leaking the backupCodesUrl object URL

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, the modal is controlled by `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>`, but the component only calls `resetState()` (and `onEnable()`) from explicit buttons: the Cancel button (steps other than `DisplayBackupCodes`) and the `backup-codes-close` button (DisplayBackupCodes step). There is no wrapper around `onOpenChange` to invoke `resetState()` when the user closes via the dialog chrome (X) or Esc/backdrop. That means internal `step`, `password`, `errorMessage`, `backupCodes`, and especially `backupCodesUrl` can remain set across closes. Additionally, `backupCodesUrl` is only revoked when a new URL is created (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), so closing via X/Esc (or even `resetState()`, which doesn’t revoke) can leak the object URL for the life of the component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts persists 10 newly generated backup codes on every password confirmation before QR scan/TOTP entry, silently invalidating previously saved backup codes if setup is abandoned

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup endpoint now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them to the user record (`data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }`) before the user completes QR scan/TOTP verification. This endpoint is called from the enable flow on password confirmation (`EnableTwoFactorModal.handleSetup`), so abandoning the flow after setup will still overwrite any existing `user.backupCodes` (and store new ones that may never be shown/confirmed), effectively invalidating prior backup codes without completing setup.
